items.title: Eddie Metz Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 3, 2015
items.q: And what had happened was Grover was listening to it on the bus and he said, “hey Basie, here, listen to this.”

ctx.x: You’re diving into the whole thing.

Yeah. You know, drinking and smoking pot and girls and all that stuff, and I was just happy going to band and playing gigs along the way. And I said hey, this isn’t terrible. Forget those classes. So eventually technically I flunked out of Eastern Michigan. So I laid off a semester and went back on my own dime, I went and found a day job, along with doing the other gigs, and got my own apartment, and went back as a music major, a music education major, taking clarinet and theory and all that stuff. And I got a…
would get that job and stay in school and just do that. And about three months after I did that I got a phone call. It was Labor Day 1982 and it was Count Basie calling me personally.
